findings.problem: Only two tests were added: the ranged caller with an unvaried start, and expanded_order invalidating the realization review. The diff has no tests for these other closures: whole-home URN caller defaults (realizations.py:306-309), uniqueness of prepared-context targets that no other unit references (realizations.py:283-286), rejection of canonical_home keys outside the whitelist (realizations.py:241-243), splitting range endpoints in the source_order/expanded_order registry traversal (build.diff:9-14), and draft pending status when another unit's realization key is stale (build.diff:23). The end-to-end build() test that round2 asked for is also still missing.
findings.fix: Add one focused test per closure. Each test should fail on the round2 code.

findings.problem: Round2 asked for the canonical_home URN to be a default target whenever the home keeps map_root or emits an idno. The code checks only map_root (default True). If a home sets map_root false but still emits an idno for its URN, a whole-file caller of that URN gets no default selection. Whether build.py emits an idno in that case is outside the inputs I read.
findings.fix: Use the same condition build.py uses to emit the home URN (map_root or idno and not omit_publication_urn), or assert that map_root false implies no addressable home URN.

notes: Ranged callers confirmed (realizations.py:330-335). When a j:transclude has targetEnd and its start identity sits in a unit with overlays, the code resolves the range through _range_segments in the document's xml:lang and collects the overlay groups of every segment, including an unvaried start. Ranges on hosts without overlays are skipped. The start segment's groups can be added twice, but this does no harm because defaults.update and the partial-selection check are idempotent.
Whole-home targets confirmed: canonical_home.urn is added when map_root is set (line 306-307), and text_corresp is still added (line 308-309).
Prepared-context uniqueness confirmed: canonical targets from every canonical_home context are added to the identity set (lines 283-286).
The EXPANDED constant is imported and used (lines 273, 290).

Home whitelist confirmed (lines 241-243). The home takes source_printings from the prepared unit. The context drops additional_printings, and the text_corresp context is prepared with wording_variants=[], so provenance stays in the home only.
Cross-language binding confirmed: the payload's variants=overlays(readings, stem) has no language filter (line 222), so both language keys bind every overlay the context's selection() declares.

expanded_order binding confirmed: a SHA256 of the canonically serialized expanded_order (sort_keys, ensure_ascii=False) is in every realization payload (line 222). This is round2 option (c). Drift in the expanded section declarations is now gated by review rather than checked structurally, which is acceptable as you chose it.
Host printing scans confirmed: realization keys now carry the overlay printings and additional_printings scans (line 223), and verify.py attaches them to page accounting (lines 56-60).

Conservative draft labels confirmed (build.diff:23). Any stale realization payload marks every realization-bearing unit's file pending. Host literal edits also invalidate the host realization payload, because the witness includes its fragments, so they are covered transitively.
Registry confirmed: source_order and expanded_order are traversed, and both endpoints of range URNs are yielded (build.diff:9-14). The import inside the generator loop works but is a style nit.

Unverified, not raised as a finding: validate_generated looks up target.partition('@')[0] directly and does not apply split_range. If any generated j:transclude ever writes a range inside @target instead of using @targetEnd, it would miss the range-default path. The generated XML was out of scope.
